source.label: Public domain — Charles H. Spurgeon, Morning and Evening (1865)

chapters.title: January — Morning Readings
chapters.content:
JANUARY 1 — MORNING
"His name shall be called Wonderful." — Isaiah 9:6

Jesus is altogether wonderful. There is no point at which you can look upon him and say, "This is ordinary." He is wonderful in his person — the Godhead joined to humanity; the eternal Son made flesh; the Almighty in the form of a servant; the infinite stooping to become a babe. He is wonderful in his offices — Prophet, Priest, and King; the Teacher of divine wisdom; the Lamb offered for sin; the Lord of heaven and earth. He is wonderful in his sufferings — what shame he bore! what grief he endured! what death he died! He is wonderful in his resurrection, his ascension, his intercession, his coming glory.

Begin this new year by fixing your eyes on Christ. Whatever the year may bring — joy or sorrow, gain or loss — he is wonderful, and he is yours. Let his wonders draw out your worship this morning.

---

JANUARY 1 — EVENING
"The LORD hath appeared of old unto me, saying, Yea, I have loved thee with an everlasting love." — Jeremiah 31:3

Note well the word "everlasting." The love of God toward his people had no beginning and will have no end. Before the foundations of the world were laid, God loved you. When the universe as yet lay sleeping in the mind of the Eternal, God had set his love upon you. Nothing you have done has made him love you more; nothing you have done has made him love you less. His love is everlasting.

Rest tonight in this great truth. When doubts assail, when sin accuses, when the heart is discouraged — come back to this. He loved you from eternity; he loves you now; he will love you to eternity. Sleep quietly in the arms of everlasting love.

---

JANUARY 2 — MORNING
"And she called the name of the LORD that spake unto her, Thou God seest me." — Genesis 16:13

Hagar had fled into the desert, alone and wretched, when God found her and spoke to her. And her response to this divine meeting was to give God a name: "Thou God seest me." This was not a statement of fear but of wonder and comfort. He sees me — even here, even in this wilderness, even in this darkness.

Child of God, as you begin this morning, remember that he sees you. He sees your situation, your fear, your need, your hope. He is not a God who is far off, who must be summoned or informed. He is the God who sees you, who has always seen you, who sees you this very moment. Let this be your comfort: you are seen by God.

---

JANUARY 2 — EVENING
"I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety." — Psalm 4:8

What a blessed pillow is this! The psalmist lays his head down not on wealth, not on human protection, not on the strength of his own arm, but on the promise of God. And because God is his protector, he sleeps in peace.

You may have many things to worry you tonight. Your circumstances may be difficult, your health uncertain, your future unclear. But here is this word: God makes you dwell in safety. Lay down your anxieties. The Lord keeps his people. He neither slumbers nor sleeps. Let him watch while you rest.

---

JANUARY 3 — MORNING
"Because of the savour of thy good ointments thy name is as ointment poured forth, therefore do the virgins love thee." — Song of Solomon 1:3

The name of Christ is the sweetest name in all the world. Say it over — Jesus. It speaks of salvation, of grace, of help, of peace. No name is like it. No sound so sweet to the ear of faith. To those who are perishing it is an unknown sound; but to those who have been saved by it, it is music and life.

Love the name of Jesus this morning. Let it be the name you carry through your day. When you meet with trials, call on it. When you meet with joy, praise it. When the day is done, let it be the last word on your lips.

---

JANUARY 3 — EVENING
"Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you." — John 14:27

Christ's farewell gift to his disciples was peace. Not prosperity, not ease, not worldly comfort — but peace. And it is a peace the world cannot give and cannot take away. It is peace with God through the blood of the cross; peace in the conscience through the witness of the Spirit; peace in the heart through the knowledge of God's everlasting love.

Do you have this peace tonight? It is not dependent on your circumstances. It does not ebb and flow with your feelings. It is the settled, deep, God-given quiet of a soul that knows itself reconciled to God and held by grace. Receive it now from the hand of the Saviour who gives it.

---

JANUARY 4 — MORNING
"Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith." — Hebrews 12:2

Looking! This is the great secret of the Christian life. Not looking to self, not looking to circumstances, not looking at other Christians — but looking to Jesus. He is the author of your faith: he gave it to you in the beginning. He is the finisher: he will perfect it to the end. Your faith began with him and will end with him.

Where are your eyes this morning? Look off everything else and look to him. When you look at yourself, you see only weakness and failure. When you look at the world, you see confusion and temptation. But when you look to Jesus — you see grace sufficient, love unchanging, power almighty, and a friend that will never leave.

---

JANUARY 4 — EVENING
"He that keepeth Israel shall neither slumber nor sleep." — Psalm 121:4

While you sleep tonight, God watches. While your eyes are closed, his eyes are open. While your hands rest, his hands hold you. The keeper of Israel never grows weary. He has no need of sleep. He watches over every one of his people every moment of every night.

Let this thought quiet your heart as you lie down. Is there some danger you are afraid of? He sees it. Is there some need you fear the morning will bring? He knows it already, and is already at work. Sleep, child of God. Your Keeper is awake.

chapters.title: February — Morning and Evening Readings
chapters.content:
FEBRUARY 1 — MORNING
"Draw me, we will run after thee." — Song of Solomon 1:4

Note the change of number: "Draw me" — singular; "we will run" — plural. This is the experience of every true Christian. When God draws him, others run with him. When a man is truly drawn by divine grace, he draws others after him. His family is influenced by his religion; his friends are affected by his conversation; his example quickens others.

Ask God to draw you nearer to himself today. A nearer walk with God will make you more useful to men. The closer you live to the sun, the more light you will reflect on those around you.

---

FEBRUARY 1 — EVENING
"I know whom I have believed, and am persuaded that he is able to keep that which I have committed unto him against that day." — 2 Timothy 1:12

Paul did not say, "I know what I have believed," but "whom I have believed." He did not rest on a creed, or a doctrine, or a system of theology, but on a Person. And knowing that Person, he was persuaded of his ability.

The Christian's confidence is not in the strength of his faith, but in the faithfulness of his Saviour. Your faith may be feeble, but Christ is able. You may have committed very little to him, but what you have committed he will keep. Rest in him tonight, not in yourself.

---

FEBRUARY 2 — MORNING
"In all their affliction he was afflicted." — Isaiah 63:9

God is not unmoved by his people's sufferings. He does not sit in heaven and watch our pain from a great distance with cool indifference. In all our afflictions he is afflicted. He feels what we feel. He enters into the sorrow of his people.

This is an astonishing truth. The almighty, infinite God — touched by the feelings of his people's infirmities. When you are in pain this morning, God is with you in it. When you are bereaved, he grieves with you. When you are tempted, he is not a high priest who cannot be touched, but one who was in all points tempted as we are.

You do not suffer alone. Go to him with your grief this morning, for he knows it already, and he cares.

---

FEBRUARY 2 — EVENING
"My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: and I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish." — John 10:27–28

"They shall never perish." This is the bedrock of the believer's security. Not some may be saved, not most will be kept — but none shall perish who are Christ's sheep. The word "never" is absolute. It admits of no exception.

Perhaps tonight you are troubled by the fear of falling, of being lost, of Christ losing you. Hear his word: you shall never perish. Not because you are strong enough to hold on, but because he is strong enough to hold you. His hand is underneath you. Sleep on this word tonight.

---

FEBRUARY 3 — MORNING
"Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven." — Matthew 5:3

The first beatitude is about poverty. Not poverty of substance — Christ does not here commend destitution — but poverty of spirit: a sense of one's own emptiness, unworthiness, and need. The man who is poor in spirit has no high thoughts of himself. He sees himself as a beggar before God.

This is the beginning of all religion. The man who thinks well of himself will not seek a Saviour. The man who sees himself as a sinner needing mercy will run to Christ. Blessed are those who feel their own unworthiness, for they will prize the grace that is free to them.

Are you poor in spirit this morning? Then the kingdom of heaven is yours.

---

FEBRUARY 3 — EVENING
"Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil: for thou art with me." — Psalm 23:4

The valley of the shadow of death is real. There are times when the Christian walks through it — through great danger, through deep sorrow, through the approach of death itself. But in that valley, he is not alone.

"Thou art with me." Not "thou art near me" or "thou art watching me" — but "with me." Present, accompanying, walking by my side. This is the word of the Good Shepherd who walks with his sheep through the darkest passages.

Whatever valley you may be passing through tonight, this is your comfort: he is with you in it.

chapters.title: March — Morning and Evening Readings
chapters.content:
MARCH 1 — MORNING
"This is a faithful saying, and worthy of all acceptation, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners; of whom I am chief." — 1 Timothy 1:15

Paul calls himself the chief of sinners. This is not false modesty — it is the language of a man who has seen himself clearly in the light of God's holiness. And yet this man is an apostle, a saint, a man indwelt by the Holy Ghost. The truth is that those who see themselves most clearly as sinners are those who have been most deeply converted.

This morning, do not be afraid of calling yourself a sinner. The gospel is for sinners. Christ came to save sinners. The greater your sense of sin, the greater your qualification for grace. Come, chief of sinners — come to the Saviour who came for you.

---

MARCH 1 — EVENING
"He restoreth my soul." — Psalm 23:3

The soul needs restoring. Even the soul of a true believer sometimes wanders from its Shepherd. It grows cold, distracted, worldly, or fearful. It strays from the green pastures into barren places. And then it needs to be brought back.

The Shepherd restores. He does not abandon the wandering sheep. He goes after it. He finds it. He brings it back. And when the soul returns to him — when the stray believer comes back to prayer, to the Word, to fellowship with God — there is a freshness and a blessing in that return.

Has your soul been wandering? He will restore it. Come back to him tonight.

---

MARCH 2 — MORNING
"Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the LORD." — Lamentations 3:40

Self-examination is a duty which many neglect. We are busy with a thousand things; we examine our accounts, our plans, our prospects. But do we examine our hearts? Do we ask ourselves, with honest searching, whether we are truly walking with God?

Here is the call of this morning: search and try your ways. Not with a morbid introspection that leads to despair, but with the honest inquiry of a soul that desires to know where it stands before God. And if the search discovers wandering, the call is not to despair but to turn — to return to the Lord.

Search yourself this morning. If you find that you have wandered, turn at once. He receives those who return.

---

MARCH 2 — EVENING
"In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world." — John 16:33

Jesus does not promise his people an easy path. He does not say, "Trust me and the world will be kind to you." He says plainly: in the world you will have tribulation. The path of the Christian is not smooth. There are thorns, and stones, and valleys, and enemies.

But the word does not end with tribulation. "Be of good cheer" — take heart, have courage. And the ground of the courage is not the hope that things will get better, but a fact already accomplished: "I have overcome the world." Christ has already fought and won. The battle is decided. The Christian is on the winning side.

Be of good cheer tonight. However hard the day has been, Christ has overcome.

---

MARCH 3 — MORNING
"The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want." — Psalm 23:1

The whole of the twenty-third psalm hangs on those opening words: "The LORD is my shepherd." If that is true, then everything else follows. Green pastures follow because a good shepherd leads to good pastures. Still waters follow because a good shepherd provides rest. The valley does not terrify because the shepherd is there.

But the great question is: is he your shepherd? Is it personal? Not merely that God is a shepherd in general, but that he is yours? Every benefit of the shepherd relationship depends on the relationship itself.

Can you say this morning, with confidence and joy: "The LORD is MY shepherd"? If you can, then you shall not want.

---

MARCH 3 — EVENING
"For I am persuaded, that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord." — Romans 8:38–39

This great passage surveys every conceivable threat to the Christian's union with God and finds each one unable to accomplish the separation. Death cannot do it. Life cannot do it. Angels, principalities, powers — none of them can do it. Things present, things to come — neither can do it. Height, depth — neither dimension of the universe can do it.

Lay this promise to your heart tonight. Whatever threatens you — whatever fear or sorrow or difficulty — none of it can separate you from the love of God in Christ. You are held by a love that is stronger than death, deeper than the grave, and higher than the heavens.

chapters.title: April — Morning and Evening Readings
chapters.content:
APRIL 1 — MORNING
"Now is Christ risen from the dead, and become the firstfruits of them that slept." — 1 Corinthians 15:20

The resurrection of Christ is the cornerstone of the Christian faith. If Christ be not risen, Paul says, then your faith is vain, you are yet in your sins, and those who have fallen asleep in Christ have perished. But Christ is risen. The tomb is empty. The grave could not hold him.

And his resurrection is the pledge and pattern of ours. He is the firstfruits — the first of many more to rise. As surely as he rose, so shall his people rise. The grave is not the end. Death is not the victor. Christ has conquered, and those who are in Christ will share his victory.

Begin this April morning with the great shout of Easter: Christ is risen! He is risen indeed!

---

APRIL 1 — EVENING
"And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever." — John 14:16

The Holy Spirit is the Comforter of God's people. When Christ departed from this world, he did not leave his people desolate. He gave them another Comforter — one who would be not just with them, as Christ was, but in them. And this Comforter abides with them forever. He does not come and go. He does not depart when we are faithless. He remains.

Are you in need of comfort tonight? The Comforter is with you. He knows your grief, your doubt, your weariness. He is ready to apply the promises of God to your heart, to draw near to you in your need, to seal upon your spirit the assurance that you are God's child.

Turn to him. Speak to him. He is with you.

---

APRIL 2 — MORNING
"I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live." — John 11:25

Christ did not merely say, "I will raise the dead," or "God will give resurrection." He said: "I am the resurrection." The resurrection is not merely something he performs — it is something he is. He is life itself. Those who are united to him share in his life.

This means that death for the Christian is not an ending but a transition. The believer does not cease to exist when he dies; he passes from the presence of death into the nearer presence of the Life himself. "Though he were dead, yet shall he live."

Live in the light of this truth today. Whatever fears you carry, whatever awareness of mortality, remember: you are united to the one who is the Resurrection and the Life.

---

APRIL 2 — EVENING
"Therefore being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ." — Romans 5:1

Peace with God — not merely peace from God, not merely peace about God, but peace with God. The enmity is gone. The war is over. The sinner who was once hostile to God and under God's wrath has been brought near by the blood of Christ and is now justified — declared righteous — and the result is peace.

Do you have this peace tonight? It is not the peace of an untroubled life, but the peace of an acquitted conscience. It is not the peace that comes from having no troubles, but the peace that comes from knowing that God is for you and not against you.

Rest in your justification. You are forgiven. You are accepted. You are at peace with God through your Lord Jesus Christ.

chapters.title: May — Morning and Evening Readings
chapters.content:
MAY 1 — MORNING
"I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing." — John 15:5

The vine and the branches. What a picture of dependence and union! The branch does not generate its own life; it receives life from the vine. It does not produce its own sap; the sap flows from the vine into it. And the result is fruit — not through the branch's own effort, but through its abiding in the vine.

This is the secret of fruitful Christian living: abiding in Christ. Not striving, not straining, not working up to some high level of spiritual effort — but abiding. Remaining connected. Staying in fellowship with him through prayer and the Word and trust.

Abide in him today. Without him you can do nothing. With him, much fruit.

---

MAY 1 — EVENING
"He that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst." — John 6:35

The promise is absolute: never hunger, never thirst. The soul that comes to Christ and believes on him will find in him a complete and permanent satisfaction. Not partial, not temporary — but complete and permanent.

The world cannot make this promise. Its pleasures satisfy for a moment and then leave you craving more. Its honors satisfy for a season and then fade. Its wealth satisfies for a time and then fails. But Christ satisfies forever.

Have you come to him? Do you believe on him? Then you shall never hunger and never thirst. Sleep tonight as one who is satisfied — satisfied by the fullness of Christ.

---

MAY 2 — MORNING
"Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you." — 1 Peter 5:7

Casting — not holding, not nursing, not accumulating — but casting. The word implies a decisive act. You pick up your care and you throw it. You transfer it from yourself to him. And the ground of this throwing is given: "for he careth for you."

God cares for you. Not in a general, abstract, impersonal way — but for you, personally, specifically. He knows your name, your situation, your need, your fear. And because he cares for you, you can cast your care on him.

Practice this casting this morning. What are you carrying? Bring it to him. Throw it to him. Let him bear it. You were not designed to carry what he is able to carry for you.

---

MAY 2 — EVENING
"The LORD bless thee, and keep thee: The LORD make his face shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee: The LORD lift up his countenance upon thee, and give thee peace." — Numbers 6:24–26

This ancient blessing has been pronounced over God's people through all the ages. Three times the name of the LORD is repeated — the blessing flows from the Father, through the Son, in the Spirit. Three blessings are given: keeping, grace, and peace.

The LORD bless you tonight — give you every good thing from his own abundance. The LORD keep you — guard you through the hours of darkness. The LORD make his face shine on you — turn toward you in favor and delight. The LORD be gracious — give you what you do not deserve. The LORD give you peace — the deep, settled quiet of a soul at rest in God.

Receive this blessing. It is for you.

chapters.title: June — Morning and Evening Readings
chapters.content:
JUNE 1 — MORNING
"The LORD is good; his mercy is everlasting; and his truth endureth to all generations." — Psalm 100:5

Here are three great truths about God that are worth meditating on as you begin a new month.

The LORD is good. Not merely good at particular times, or good to particular people, but essentially, inherently, absolutely good. His goodness is not a quality he sometimes has — it is what he is. Everything he does is good, even when we cannot understand it.

His mercy is everlasting. It has no end. It will outlast time itself. Those who are the objects of his mercy will find that mercy still flowing at the last day, and through all eternity.

His truth endures to all generations. He does not change his word. The promises made to Abraham are still valid. The promises made in the Psalms are still valid. The promises made by Christ are still valid. His truth endures.

Start June with these three foundations under you.

---

JUNE 1 — EVENING
"There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus." — Romans 8:1

"No condemnation" — what words of freedom these are! No condemnation. Not little condemnation, not reduced condemnation, but no condemnation at all. The believer in Christ stands before God completely clear. The verdict has been given: not guilty.

This is the wonder of justification. The sinner has sinned. The law condemns him. But Christ has borne the condemnation. Christ has paid the debt. And now, in Christ, there is no condemnation left to fall on the sinner who believes.

Go to sleep tonight under this verdict. Whatever your conscience may say, whatever memories of sin may arise, whatever the accuser may whisper — the Word of God speaks louder: no condemnation. You are in Christ. You are free.

---

JUNE 2 — MORNING
"The eternal God is thy refuge, and underneath are the everlasting arms." — Deuteronomy 33:27

Underneath are the everlasting arms. Not beside you, not above you — though God is those things too — but underneath you. Supporting you from below. Keeping you from sinking.

The believer may feel at times as though he is falling. His faith may weaken. His strength may fail. Circumstances may press down on him until he feels he is sinking. But underneath are the everlasting arms. He cannot fall through. God is beneath him.

Go through today with this assurance. Whatever sinks, you cannot sink through God. His arms are under you and they are everlasting.

---

JUNE 2 — EVENING
"He that spared not his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not with him also freely give us all things?" — Romans 8:32

Here is a magnificent argument from the greater to the lesser. God gave his Son — the greatest gift possible, the most costly gift conceivable. If he gave that, what lesser thing will he withhold? If he gave his own Son, will he withhold bread, or health, or comfort, or grace, or any needful thing?

The cross is the guarantee of every blessing. Having done the hardest thing — having given his Son to die — God will not fail to do the easier things. He who gave Christ will give all things needful with him.

Rest tonight on the logic of the cross. He who did not spare his Son will spare you nothing good.

chapters.title: July — Morning and Evening Readings
chapters.content:
JULY 1 — MORNING
"The name of the LORD is a strong tower: the righteous runneth into it, and is safe." — Proverbs 18:10

When danger comes, where do you run? Some run to human help — to friends, to wealth, to their own abilities. But the righteous man runs to a stronger refuge: the name of the LORD.

The name of the LORD represents all that God is — his power, his faithfulness, his love, his sovereignty. To run into his name is to shelter in all that he is. And those who shelter there are safe — not merely safer, not merely less exposed, but safe.

Run to him today. Whatever threatens you this morning — run to his name. It is a strong tower, and there is room for you in it.

---

JULY 1 — EVENING
"God is our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble." — Psalm 46:1

A very present help — not a help that must be fetched from far away, not a help that requires long preparation, but a help that is very present, immediately available, close at hand.

When trouble comes, God does not need to be summoned from a great distance. He is already there. He is present in the trouble with his people. He is a help that is available the moment it is needed.

Whatever trouble you are in tonight, he is in it with you as a present help. Lean on him. Cry to him. He is there.

---

JULY 2 — MORNING
"For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the glory which shall be revealed in us." — Romans 8:18

Here is Paul's comfort in suffering: he compares it to what is coming. And when he does the comparison, the suffering shrinks. Not that the suffering is not real — Paul suffered greatly. But the glory to be revealed is so much greater that the comparison itself becomes almost comical.

Look at your sufferings today in the light of eternity. Weigh them against the weight of glory that is coming. This is not wishful thinking — it is Paul's deliberate reckoning, his considered calculation, his theological conclusion.

Suffer with patience. Compare with hope. The glory that is coming is not worthy to be compared with the sufferings of this present time — or rather, the sufferings are not worthy to be compared with the glory.

---

JULY 2 — EVENING
"My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness." — 2 Corinthians 12:9

Paul had a thorn in the flesh. Three times he prayed for it to be removed. And God's answer was not removal but provision: "My grace is sufficient."

Sufficient — enough, adequate, more than enough. Whatever the thorn, grace is enough for it. Whatever the weakness, grace can sustain through it. God did not promise Paul the removal of the difficulty but the sufficiency of grace for it.

What is your thorn tonight? What weakness or suffering has not been removed despite prayer? Hear the same answer that came to Paul: My grace is sufficient. It is enough. Trust it.

chapters.title: August — Morning and Evening Readings
chapters.content:
AUGUST 1 — MORNING
"Whosoever will, let him take the water of life freely." — Revelation 22:17

Freedom! The offer of the gospel is perfectly free. There are no conditions of worthiness, no prior qualifications of goodness, no payment required. Whosoever will — any person who desires — may come and take the water of life freely.

The only requirement is willingness. And even that willingness is the gift of God's Spirit, drawing men to Christ. But the offer is indiscriminate: whoever will may come. No one is turned away. No one is told they are too sinful, too far gone, too long delayed.

Come this morning, whatever your condition. If you are willing — if you desire salvation, if you desire Christ — come. The water of life is free.

---

AUGUST 1 — EVENING
"I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee." — Hebrews 13:5

Five negatives in the original Greek — I will never, never, never, never, never leave or forsake you. The strongest possible statement of the permanence of God's presence with his people.

You may feel alone tonight. You may be in a dark place, a lonely place, a frightening place. But God's word stands: he will not leave you. He will not forsake you. He was there before your trouble began and he will be there when it is over.

Not circumstances, not feelings, not sin, not failure — nothing can remove the presence of the God who has pledged himself to his people with five-fold negatives. He is with you. He will not leave.

---

AUGUST 2 — MORNING
"Lord, teach us to pray." — Luke 11:1

The disciples did not ask Jesus to teach them to preach, or to work miracles, or to fast — they asked him to teach them to pray. They had seen him pray, and they wanted what he had.

Prayer is the most important business of the Christian's day. More is accomplished through prayer than through all our other activities combined. Yet it is the thing most neglected, most rushed through, most treated as a formality.

Ask this same thing today: Lord, teach me to pray. Not just to say prayers, but to pray — to actually speak with God, to seek his face, to lay your needs before him, to wait for his answer. The disciples learned from the best teacher. So may we.

---

AUGUST 2 — EVENING
"He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty." — Psalm 91:1

The secret place of the most High — this is the place of close, intimate fellowship with God. Not the public court, not the outer courts, but the secret place. The place of private prayer, of Bible reading done not as duty but as fellowship, of the soul waiting quietly on God.

Those who dwell there — who make it their habitual residence, who are at home in God's presence — shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty. The shadow of the Almighty is a place of protection and rest. It is cool in the heat of trial, sheltering in the storm of temptation.

Dwell in the secret place. Make it your home. Then the shadow of the Almighty will be your covering.

chapters.title: September — Morning and Evening Readings
chapters.content:
SEPTEMBER 1 — MORNING
"But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you." — Matthew 6:33

First. This word is all-important. Not God alongside your other priorities, not God mixed in with everything else, but God first. Seek his kingdom first. Seek his righteousness first. Give him the priority of your morning, your affection, your ambition, your plans.

And then note the promise: all these things shall be added. The "things" in context are food, drink, and clothing — the necessities of life. Christ is not promising luxury or ease. He is promising that those who seek God first will find that God provides what they need.

Make God first this morning. In your prayer, in your thinking, in your decisions for this day. He will add what is needed.

---

SEPTEMBER 1 — EVENING
"And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus." — Philippians 4:7

The peace of God — not peace about God, not peace with God (though that is elsewhere promised), but the peace of God himself. The peace that God himself has. A peace that passes all understanding.

This peace guards the heart and mind as a garrison guards a city. It keeps out the invading forces of anxiety and despair. It holds the believer steady when circumstances are turbulent.

And this peace comes through what? Paul has told us in the preceding verses: through prayer, through thanksgiving, through bringing every anxiety to God. The peace of God fills the space vacated by anxiety.

Pray your anxieties away tonight. In their place, receive the peace that passes understanding.

---

SEPTEMBER 2 — MORNING
"Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you." — Matthew 7:7

Three pictures of prayer, each more intense than the last. Asking — a simple request. Seeking — active pursuit. Knocking — persistent pressing at the door. And to each, a promise: given, found, opened.

God invites persistence in prayer. He is not glorified by our quick, casual petitions that we mention once and forget. He is glorified by the persistent, earnest, believing prayer of a soul that will not let go.

Ask today. And if no answer comes, seek. And if still no answer comes, knock. The door will be opened. God has promised.

---

SEPTEMBER 2 — EVENING
"Now unto him that is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think, according to the power that worketh in us, unto him be glory." — Ephesians 3:20

Exceeding abundantly above all that we ask or think. What a God we have! He does not give us exactly what we ask, or approximately what we ask. He gives exceeding abundantly above all that we ask.

Our asking is limited by our imagination. Our imagination is limited by our knowledge. Our knowledge is limited by our creaturely finitude. But God is not limited by any of these things. He can do more than our largest prayer, our boldest request, our most ambitious faith.

Ask largely tonight. But trust that God will do more than you have asked.

chapters.title: October — Morning and Evening Readings
chapters.content:
OCTOBER 1 — MORNING
"Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me." — Psalm 51:10

This is the prayer of a man who has sinned greatly and knows it. David, after his terrible fall, does not pray for the consequences to be removed, or for things to return to what they were. He prays for something far more fundamental: a clean heart, a right spirit.

He knows that the problem is not merely what he did, but what he is. And so he prays not for a patch job but for a new creation: "Create in me." The word is the word used for God's creating the world. What David needs is not reform but re-creation.

This is always the deepest need. Come to God this morning with this prayer: Create in me a clean heart. Renew a right spirit. Whatever yesterday was, let today begin with this.

---

OCTOBER 1 — EVENING
"God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape." — 1 Corinthians 10:13

With the temptation — a way to escape. Not after the temptation, not before the temptation, but with it. At the same moment the temptation arrives, God has already provided the way out.

No temptation is inescapable. There is always a way out. God has not allowed any temptation to come to you without first preparing an escape route. The question is whether you will take it.

Were you tempted today? Did you look for the way of escape? Tonight, ask God to help you see the exits he has prepared, and to take them tomorrow.

---

OCTOBER 2 — MORNING
"Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path." — Psalm 119:105

A lamp to my feet — illuminating the very next step. A light to my path — illuminating the road ahead. The Word of God does both: it gives guidance for the immediate step and direction for the longer journey.

We live in a dark world. We face decisions we cannot resolve by our own wisdom. We walk through situations that confuse and perplex us. We need light.

God's Word is that light. Not human wisdom, not the wisdom of the age, not even the best counsel of the wisest friends — but the Word of God. Read it today. Meditate on it. Let it light your path.

---

OCTOBER 2 — EVENING
"For our light and momentary troubles are achieving for us an eternal glory that far outweighs them all." — 2 Corinthians 4:17

Light and momentary. Paul is speaking of things which included beatings, imprisonment, shipwreck, hunger, sleeplessness, and the constant burden of all the churches. And he calls them light and momentary. Not because they are not real, not because they do not hurt, but because compared to the eternal weight of glory — they are light.

This is the gospel perspective on suffering: not denial of the pain, but comparison with the coming glory. The comparison renders the suffering light. Not nothing — but light.

Look at your sufferings tonight from eternity. They are working something. They are achieving for you an eternal glory that far outweighs them all.

chapters.title: November — Morning and Evening Readings
chapters.content:
NOVEMBER 1 — MORNING
"Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who hath blessed us with all spiritual blessings in heavenly places in Christ." — Ephesians 1:3

All spiritual blessings. Not some — all. Not the lesser ones — all, including the greatest. Election, adoption, redemption, forgiveness, sealing with the Spirit, the guarantee of inheritance — all these are yours in Christ.

Begin this November by counting your spiritual blessings. Not your material blessings — those are good but they are fewer and more variable. Count your spiritual blessings: you are forgiven, you are adopted, you are sealed with the Spirit, you are an heir of glory. All these are yours — in Christ.

Blessed be God for them this morning.

---

NOVEMBER 1 — EVENING
"And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God." — Revelation 21:3

This is the final destination. Heaven is not primarily a place of ease, or of beautiful scenery, or of reunions with loved ones. Heaven is where God dwells with his people. Heaven is the perfect and eternal fulfillment of what began at Sinai, continued in the temple, was embodied in the incarnation, and is now present through the Spirit.

God with us — permanently, fully, without the veil, without the cloud, face to face. This is heaven. This is what is coming.

Let this encourage you tonight. Whatever this world has denied you, heaven will exceed it. Whatever grief this life has brought, heaven will more than answer it. God himself will be with you there.

---

NOVEMBER 2 — MORNING
"I press toward the mark for the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus." — Philippians 3:14

Pressing. This is not relaxed Christian living. Paul is pressing — straining forward, reaching toward the goal. He has not arrived. He is not coasting. He is pressing.

The Christian life is not a life of passive enjoyment. It is a life of active pursuit. There is a prize to be won, a race to be run, a mark to be reached. The Christian is not merely surviving until heaven — he is running toward it.

Press today. Do not drift. Do not loosen your grip on the things of God. Do not allow the world to lull you into spiritual laziness. Press toward the mark.

---

NOVEMBER 2 — EVENING
"He which testifieth these things saith, Surely I come quickly. Amen. Even so, come, Lord Jesus." — Revelation 22:20

The last prayer of the Bible. Christ says: Surely I come quickly. And the response of the church is: Even so, come, Lord Jesus. Amen.

Do you have this longing tonight? Do you desire the coming of Christ? Is there in your heart a genuine looking for him, a readiness to see him, a gladness at the thought of his return?

This longing is a mark of the true believer. Those who love his appearing are those who love him. And those who love him live with their faces turned toward his coming.

Even so, come, Lord Jesus.

chapters.title: December — Morning and Evening Readings
chapters.content:
DECEMBER 1 — MORNING
"Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." — Isaiah 7:14

Immanuel — God with us. This is the great mystery of Christmas: that the eternal God became flesh and dwelt among us. Not an angel, not a representative, not a prophet — but God himself, in human form, in a human body, born of a woman, lying in a manger.

This is the most astonishing event in history. Heaven stooped to earth. Infinity became finite. The eternal entered time. And the name he bore told the reason: Immanuel — God with us.

With us. Not above us, not merely for us, but with us. He entered our condition. He took on our nature. He walked our roads, felt our cold, tasted our grief. God with us.

Begin this December with worship at the mystery of the incarnation.

---

DECEMBER 1 — EVENING
"For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life." — John 3:16

This is the most famous verse in the Bible, and it cannot be exhausted. God — the Almighty, the sovereign Creator. So loved — not merely liked, not merely regarded with benevolence, but loved with the most profound love possible. The world — the sinful, rebellious, God-rejecting world. That he gave — at cost, at infinite cost. His only begotten Son — not a servant, not a prophet, but his own Son.

That whosoever believes in him should not perish but have everlasting life. The gift is for any who believe. The result is life — everlasting life, the life of God himself, given to those who trust in Christ.

Rest in this verse tonight. It holds everything.

---

DECEMBER 25 — MORNING
"And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth." — John 1:14

The Word was made flesh. What a sentence! The eternal Word — by whom all things were made, who was in the beginning with God, who was God — was made flesh. He became what he had never been before. He took upon himself a human nature, a human body, a human experience.

And he dwelt among us. The Greek word means "tabernacled" — he pitched his tent among us. As the tabernacle in the wilderness was the place where God dwelt among his people, so Christ was God's tabernacle on earth.

And those who were with him beheld his glory — the glory of the Father's only Son, full of grace and truth. This is what Christmas is. Not sentiment, not custom — but the incarnation of the eternal Son of God. Worship him this morning.

---

DECEMBER 25 — EVENING
"Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men." — Luke 2:14

The angels' song at Christmas. Glory to God — for in the birth of this child, God has done something worthy of his greatest glory. He has found a way to be just and the justifier of the ungodly. He has found a way to redeem without compromise. He has given his Son.

And on earth peace — peace between God and man, made possible by the one who has come to be the mediator, the reconciler, the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.

Good will toward men — not because men deserve it, but because God in his sovereign grace has determined to show mercy to men through his Son.

Glory to God tonight. Receive his peace. Rest in his good will toward you.

---

DECEMBER 31 — MORNING
"The LORD hath been mindful of us: he will bless us." — Psalm 115:12

As this year ends, look back and testify: the LORD has been mindful of us. Through all the days of this year — the good days and the hard ones, the days of health and the days of sickness, the days of joy and the days of grief — the LORD has been mindful.

Not a day has passed without his notice. Not a moment has escaped his care. He has been mindful of you this entire year.

And now look forward: he will bless us. The one who has been faithful through the past year will be faithful in the year to come. His mercies do not end at December 31. They are new every morning. He will bless.

---

DECEMBER 31 — EVENING
"Even to your old age I am he; and even to hoar hairs will I carry you: I have made, and I will bear; even I will carry, and will deliver you." — Isaiah 46:4

As this year ends and another begins, here is God's word for all the years that remain: I will carry you. Through youth and age, through strength and weakness, through health and decline — I will carry you.

You may not know what the new year holds. But you know who holds the new year. The same God who has carried you through every year of your life will carry you through the next.

Close your eyes tonight under this promise. He made you. He will carry you. He will deliver you. Even to the end.
